title: Trivial Event Handlers (Simple Forwarding Listeners)
pattern: Creating custom handler classes or structs that do nothing but catch an event and forward it directly to an underlying dispatcher or processor.
why_bad: It introduces useless class and method ceremony. It clutters the event pipeline with shallow pass-through components, forcing developers to wade through multiple empty call frames to see how an event is actually processed.
detection: A listener or event handler implementation whose handler methods consist solely of a direct forwarding call with zero preprocessing or condition checks.
counterexample: Event handlers that serialize events, append analytical telemetry, or conditionally route events based on payload types.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Code Smells - Middle Man"), p. 81.
